name: spec-layout
description: The spec file reads chronologically: one canonical layout

research.description: Field-order precedents (JSON:API, GitHub API, package.json, OpenAPI, RFC 8259/8785) and the mechanical facts

clarifications.answer: Metadata sits sixth and means the generic external-reference layer: Jira issues, Confluence pages, GitHub tickets, files, anything (owner, 2026-10-09: the source of a spec can be anything, so it stays generic). The machine's own bookkeeping (format, revision, env) moves to the tail, last, per the JSON:API/npm/OpenAPI precedent.
clarifications.question: Metadata position: sixth per the owner's list, or last per the JSON:API/npm/OpenAPI precedent (meta as the residual bucket)?

constraints.text: Frozen specs never rewrite: dual-read, no migration-in-place.
Digests stay deterministic: sorted-key canonical form for hashing, authored order for the file.

scenarios.then: the top-level keys appear in the canonical order, exactly, every time

requirements.text: The writer MUST emit the file in one canonical order: id, name, description, date, status, metadata, spec, design, tasks, review; nested content keeps its own documented order. Digests keep sorted-key hashing (two orders, two jobs, per RFC 8785).

scenarios.given: a frozen spec in the old layout
scenarios.then: it loads through the normalizer and its bytes never change

requirements.text: Renames with dual-read: title becomes description, plan becomes design, artifacts generalizes into metadata (the external-reference registry: entry key to a ref that may be a URL or a path), closed_by and closed_at move into date.closed {at, by}, and format, revision, env move to the tail, after review. The loader accepts both layouts (old keys normalize in memory; new keys pass through); the writer emits only the new layout. Frozen specs are never rewritten and load forever.

The header carries id, date, and status groups: id (the slug), date {created author-supplied, updated machine-stamped at each save, closed from the close command}, status {lifecycle, deliverable}. A machine-stamped date.updated is document metadata, amending the no-clocks rule for header dates only; loop event data keeps caller-supplied clocks.
This spec migrates itself as the first fixture once the loader supports the new layout, and the three frozen specs (specpack-context, status-vocabulary, status-model) stay byte-identical.

metadata MUST be the generic external-reference registry: keyed entries carrying ref (URL or path), type, description, and an optional sha256 pin. Jira issues, Confluence pages, tickets, and the Feature Brief register here. The machine verifies pinned refs at handout as it verifies artifacts today.

stories.as: a person opening a spec file
stories.so: I understand the deliverable without hunting through an alphabetical key dump
stories.want: to read it top to bottom like a dossier: identity, dates, status, then spec, design, tasks, review

stories.as: a future loop reading many spec files
stories.so: my eyes and my tools land in the same place every time
stories.want: one identical layout on every file, old and new

spec.why: The spec file is written with sorted keys, so it reads alphabetically: artifacts, closed_at, closed_by, deliverable, format... The organization is the problem, not the JSON. A person opening the file must read what it is, when, where it stands, and then the content in the order it was produced.

design.approach: One canonical layout, dual-read loader, self-migration as the first fixture. The writer controls emission order; nothing else in the ecosystem reads it.

decisions.because: RFC 8259 gives order no machine meaning, so its only value is human; the field consensus (JSON:API, GitHub, npm, OpenAPI) front-loads identity, chronology, and status before content in production order.
decisions.decision: One canonical reading order, emitted by the writer at every save: id, name, description, date, status, metadata (external references), spec, design, tasks, review, then the machine tail (env, format, revision).

decisions.because: A cosmetic reading fix must not break three frozen reference specs or every existing file.
decisions.decision: Renames ride a dual-read normalizer; frozen specs load forever, never rewrite.

decisions.because: okf already stamps generated.at; a reader asks when this file was last true. The amendment is scoped to the header.
decisions.decision: date.updated is machine-stamped at save (UTC); date.created is author-supplied; date.closed comes from the close command. Header dates are document metadata; the no-clocks rule still governs loop event data.

decisions.because: The RFC 8785 pattern: two orders, two jobs. Determinism of digests is untouched by reading order.
decisions.decision: Digests hash the sorted-key canonical copy; the file keeps authored order.

decisions.because: Owner, 2026-10-09: metadata is for additional links like Jira issues and Confluence pages; the source can be anything, so the registry stays generic. The precedents' meta-last applies to machine bookkeeping, which moves to the tail instead.
decisions.decision: metadata is the generic external-reference registry: keyed entries of ref (URL or path), type, description, optional sha256. It generalizes the artifacts registry (files were always one kind of reference) and it is where the Feature Brief registers. Machine bookkeeping (format, revision, env) is NOT metadata; it lives at the tail.

designs.detail: Emission order: id, name, description, date {created, updated, closed {at, by}}, status {lifecycle, deliverable}, metadata {<key>: {ref, type, description, sha256?}} (external references: Jira, Confluence, tickets, files, the Feature Brief), spec, design, tasks, review, then the machine tail: env, format, revision. The writer builds the dict in this order and serializes without top-level sort_keys; digest hashing keeps sort_keys on the canonicalized copy.
designs.title: The canonical layout and the ordered writer

designs.detail: load_specpack normalizes: old title -> description, plan -> design, top-level artifacts -> metadata (entry key file -> ref; files were always references), closed_by/closed_at -> date.closed {at, by}, flat status/deliverable -> status group, format/revision/env -> tail fields. In-memory shape is always the new layout; the old file on disk is untouched. The checksum (deliverable) check runs after normalization.
designs.title: Dual-read normalizer

designs.detail: Once the loader accepts the new layout, this spec file is recast into it (id, date.created, status group, metadata group, design key) and re-checked green; the frozen specs are byte-compared before and after the whole wave.
designs.title: Self-migration fixture

Tests: emission order exact on save; old-layout fixture loads to the new in-memory shape; bytes of the source never change.

findings.note: T-3's evidence row claims exit 0 and 'check 0/0', but loom check had REFUSED ('not a spec: missing spec, plan, or tasks'): cmd_check loaded the file raw, bypassing the dual-read normalizer, and the shell chain's wc -l rescued the exit status. The record went in false. Third instance of the pipe-masked-exit class.
findings.fix: cmd_check now loads through load_specpack (normalizer); the defect and this disclosure are recorded here per the T-4 precedent.

findings.note: validate ran on the internal mixed form (id/created/updated absent from oldRoot) and failed both anyOf branches.
findings.fix: oldRoot extended additively with id, created, updated; the schema is the file contract and the internal form validates as oldRoot.
